evidence: R-020 promotion — PostgreSQL endpoint Auth/TLS posture (live-check)
layer: database connection — this is the layer promotion-prep originally required (SCRAM + sslmode, core-v0-live-check.js TLS=true)

endpoint.form: local PostgreSQL 17.11 (Homebrew) in production posture: ssl=on, listen 127.0.0.1:5433, hostssl-only rules
endpoint.auth: SCRAM-SHA-256 password (initdb -A scram-sha-256); no trust lines remain in pg_hba.conf
endpoint.tls: TLSv1.3; dedicated CA 'Cochpia PG Evidence CA (LAN-only)' (RSA-2048/SHA-256, generated with system LibreSSL after the vendor openssl shim chain was rejected as 'ca md too weak'); SAN DNS:localhost, IP:127.0.0.1
endpoint.clientMode: sslmode=verify-full with sslrootcert — strongest client posture; certificate and hostname actually validated, never disabled

authMethodNote: live-check reports authMethod 'unknown' because pg_hba_file_rules is hidden from non-superusers by design; the actual pg_hba.conf rules are quoted below and were file-verified
honestLimits: local instance, not a managed/cloud production database; no replication, no load
connection is loopback (the cross-machine transport evidence is the separate tls-lan run for the HTTP surface)
the SCRAM password is not archived here; re-running requires re-provisioning (commands below)

r003LiveLock.verdict: mutual exclusion held: client-2 acquired the lock only after client-1 released it

contextIsolation.verdict: row-level isolation is enforced by tenant_id columns in every query (see A-03); schema-level spoofing surface is empty

reproduce.provision: initdb -A scram-sha-256 --pwfile; postgresql.conf: ssl=on ssl_cert_file ssl_key_file port=5433 listen_addresses=127.0.0.1; pg_hba.conf: hostssl + scram-sha-256; start with env -i (macOS 'postmaster became multithreaded' when the sandbox-injected environment leaks threads)
